title: Deliberative design decision: choose among declared options against declared criteria, with recorded objections

fixture.question: Which on-disk format should the eval harness use for a trial's event log: JSONL, SQLite, or a columnar file? Constraints: no new runtime dependency, append-only writes during a run, readable with standard tools after a crash, queries by role and time range for reports.
fixture.note: Spec section 9.1 defers deliberative sections; this scenario runs with separate deliberative roles, as today.

units.description: A decision record: the options, each criterion scored per option with a one-line reason, the chosen option and why it wins
units.evidence: all three mandatory options and all five criteria are present; every option has a score and reason per criterion; the chosen option has the highest total (machine check)

units.description: The objections raised by at least two distinct roles, each with its disposition (accepted, rejected with reason, or deferred)
units.evidence: at least two roles are named; every objection has a disposition; each rejected objection has a stated reason

completion_rule: Both units present and accepted, and the record's chosen option matches the option the objection log's final disposition leaves standing. Adding options or criteria beyond the declared ones adds nothing.

criteria.description: The chosen option follows from the record's own scores
Every mandatory option and criterion is evaluated
Objections are real (they change a score or are answered on the merits), not agreement restated
Claims about each format's behaviour are true

critical_failures: a chosen option that contradicts the record's own scoring
a mandatory option or criterion missing
a claim about a format that is false and changes a score

allowed_recovery: automatic restart of a crashed role within the runtime's retry limits
one operator answer to a blocking question, recorded as an intervention

primary_comparisons: cost per accepted unit, candidate vs matched baseline, paired by run
probability of a fully accepted fixture, with its Wilson interval
objections that changed a score, per run
